headline: Senate Republicans lost 7 seats. Thune stays.
summary: Senate Republicans reelected John Thune of South Dakota as their leader Tuesday, a week after an election that cost them at least seven seats and the majority. He ran unopposed in a secret ballot. Ron Johnson and Josh Hawley wanted a delay to think it over. The conference voted to proceed, and both walked out. Trump stayed out of it.

cover_question.q: Lose that badly and keep the boss?

cover_answer: Nobody else ran. 'Who would want the job?'
table_question: If the whole team loses, is it the captain's fault?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The Republicans in the Senate lost a lot of seats in last week's election, so they are the smaller team now. On Tuesday they voted to keep the same captain, John Thune from South Dakota. Some wanted a timeout to think first, like a team that lost asking for a minute. Nothing changes at our house.
5-7.why: A team that lost and kept its captain: the whole story at this age. The filibuster stays out.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a team that lost and kept its captain, which they have seen on a field, and a timeout they have asked for themselves. Expect 'did he get in trouble?' No. His teammates said the loss wasn't his fault, and they voted to keep him.

8-12.script: Republicans lost at least seven Senate seats, so in January they lose the majority. Before that, each party picks its leaders. Some senators wanted a delay, like calling a timeout before a big call. The group voted to go ahead, and John Thune, running alone, kept the job.
8-12.why: A loss, a timeout request, a vote anyway: a chain they can argue with.
8-12.why_long: At 11 they are working out rules and whether adults apply them, so the script hands over the chain: a loss, a request for a timeout, a vote to go ahead anyway, a ballot with one name on it. The timeout is the mechanism they know. Expect 'why did nobody else run?' The senators themselves said no one wants the job. Say so.

13-17.script: Lose seven seats and keep the same boss? Senate Republicans did on Tuesday: John Thune ran unopposed and won. Johnson and Hawley asked for a delay. Hawley asked what rushing it says. Second: if nobody else wants the job, is that a reason to keep someone, or a problem on its own?
13-17.why: Unopposed and under fire, both true. Is an empty ballot confidence?
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Thune won every vote cast, and his party lost at least seven seats under him. The script asks whether an empty ballot is confidence or a shrug, and at 13 they are testing whether you will argue it honestly. Expect 'what did he do wrong?' Colleagues say the loss wasn't his. Say so.

5-7.q: Why vote if only one person ran?
5-7.a: That's the rule. Even one name gets a vote, so everyone has a say. Like voting on pizza when pizza is the only choice.

8-12.q: Why not wait and think about it?
8-12.a: Johnson and Hawley wanted to. Most said the new senators were in town.

8-12.q: Did he lose the election for them?
8-12.a: Senators said no, the leaders didn't cause it. Thune: a tough night.

13-17.q: Lose that badly and keep the boss?
13-17.a: Nobody else ran. Senators say Thune listens, and the loss wasn't his.

13-17.q: What does it say that nobody else ran?
13-17.a: Lankford said it aloud. Thankless job, or nobody wants to own the loss?
